items.manifestation: After the recurrence threshold state is entered, every later correction request returns an error for the remainder of that session branch.
When the terminal recurrence state rejects an action, the error does not identify which aggregate group triggered that state.
Appending one event copies every earlier event, so total copy work grows quadratically with history length.
Two otherwise identical records whose abstraction text differs only by capitalization produce separate aggregate groups.
The formatter’s generated output cannot reach the configured truncation threshold under its practical output bounds.
A record added late for a commit that predates a correction is counted as a later recurrence because processing follows insertion order.
A branch tests whether at least one occurrence exists in a state where the surrounding operation cannot exist without a prior occurrence.
State restoration compares serialized event objects, so acceptance depends on object-key ordering surviving the storage round trip.
Every distinct abstraction description is concatenated into one display field without a length or item bound.
The same correction commit can be recorded again under a different descriptive abstraction and can advance the recurrence counter as if two distinct corrections occurred.
An unresolved record from an earlier commit is displayed in a collection named stale findings.
A test remains passing when a runtime export used by the extension is unavailable under its expected name.
When more than one aggregate group meets the reporting condition, the result includes only the first group.
A terminal recurrence state reached by one aggregate group prevents correction requests for unrelated groups.
A historical event successfully written under one validation rule set can cause state restoration to fail after those rules change.
Two open records that differ only in descriptive abstraction text require separate correction events even though occurrence aggregation treats them as one category.
The system computes four head-based finding partitions that the recurrence decision does not read.
After an earlier observation is closed, its review commit identifier can later be recorded as a correction commit identifier.
A full-package one-function test double causes later unstubbed runtime imports to resolve to an undefined value in tests.
Two abstraction descriptions containing commas can produce the same comma-joined display text as a different list of descriptions.
Restoration recomputes the expected record identifiers before a canonical event comparison repeats the same mismatch check.
The extension exports thirteen symbols that no consumer imports.
The set reported as current-head findings changes according to the commit identifier of the event just recorded rather than an independently supplied repository head.
After any historical event fails restoration, a read-only status request returns an error along with state-changing requests.
